rounds.proof_sketch: size=262144, threads=65536, max_idx=262140. Original: idx+3<size gives 262143<262144=TRUE for all threads. Mutated: idx-3<size gives -3 to 262137 < 262144=TRUE for all threads. Both conditions evaluate identically for all launched threads.
rounds.survival_reason: The fixed shape [16,16384] results in size=262144 elements. The vectorized kernel launches exactly 65536 threads (256 blocks × 256 threads), each processing 4 elements. Since 65536×4=262144, every thread processes exactly 4 valid elements. The maximum thread (tid=65535) has idx=262140 and accesses indices 262140-262143, all within bounds. Both the original condition (idx+3<size=262143<262144) and the mutated condition (idx-3<size=262137<262144) evaluate to TRUE for all threads. No thread ever reaches the slow path in either version, making the mutation behaviorally equivalent for this exact configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: The mutation cannot be killed with the fixed shape [16,16384]. The size 262144 perfectly divides by 4 and exactly matches the maximum thread coverage (65536 threads × 4 elements), so all threads legitimately use the fast path in both original and mutated versions.
rounds.recommendations: Add explicit boundary tests with sizes that don't perfectly match thread coverage, e.g., sizes where size/4 is not exactly equal to the launched thread count, to ensure remainder-handling code paths are exercised.
